title: Seva, reviewed
tomorrow: a college tour, three states from home. who'd help her remember?

segments.voice: Yesterday, seva with neighbors: no enemy, no stranger, and a Muslim saint's verses inside the Granth. Serve together. Two weeks of seva now: the gurdwara, the food bank, the sick, the elders, the creek. Time to choose.
screen: `SERVE TOGETHER.` → `TWO WEEKS OF SEVA. NOW CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Simran's calendar looks like a game of Tetris losing badly. Creek on Saturdays, food bank on Tuesdays, tutoring on Thursdays, and a chemistry grade sliding. At dinner Harjit says, pick one and keep it. Bebe, passing the dal, says, then pick the shoes. Joray seva, at the gurdwara, Sunday mornings, where you started. Harjit says the world needs her more than the shoe rack does. Bebe raises one eyebrow. Two people Simran loves, two answers.
screen: `A CALENDAR LOSING AT TETRIS.` → `DAD: OUT IN THE WORLD.` → `BEBE: THE SHOES, AT THE GURDWARA.`

segments.voice: Both views live inside Sikhi, so let each speak. Harjit's case first. On Ang 26 Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: in the midst of this world, do seva, and you'll be given a seat in the Lord's court. In the world. Not after it, not apart from it. The food bank is the world. The creek is the world. If seva stays behind the gurdwara doors, the hungry on Tuesday wait. Now Bebe's case. The gurdwara is where seva is learned. Wiping the shoes of strangers who'll never know your name, in the Guru's presence, with the sangat beside you, scrubs at haumai, the I, I, I, in a way a volunteer badge might not. And the sangat runs on it: no hands, no langar. Seva in the Guru's house is training for seva everywhere else. Each is a real view Sikhs hold, and some hold both. Simran hears them out, then tries a month of two: the food bank with Maya on Tuesdays, and the shoe rack with Bebe on Sundays. Tutoring and the creek go to friends who've got more room. My seva doesn't have to be everything. It has to be kept.
screen: `ANG 26: SEVA IN THE MIDST OF THE WORLD.` · `THE WORLD IS WHERE THE NEED IS.` · `THE GURDWARA IS WHERE SEVA IS LEARNED.` · `A MONTH OF TWO, KEPT.` · then, large: `MY SEVA.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper. Write one line by hand: the one seva you could keep, and the day it happens. Then hold the paper for the sit and read your own handwriting slowly, once at the start and once at the end.
Seva. Selfless service, done for others with no wage, in the gurdwara and in the world.
For the road: my seva, small enough to keep and real enough to count. Day 1711, chosen.

screen: `DAY 1711 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 85 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: THREE STATES FROM HOME. WHO HELPS HER REMEMBER?`

fork.setup: Simran leans toward her dad's view. what's the strongest case she could make for Bebe's side?
options: the gurdwara is where seva is learned: strangers' shoes, the Guru's presence, haumai scrubbed.
Bebe's generation is just more used to the gurdwara, so it feels right to her.
the food bank isn't really seva, because it isn't run by a gurdwara.
fork.reveal: Bebe's best case isn't habit: it's that seva in the Guru's house trains the self, and the sangat runs on those hands. Harjit's best case is Ang 26.
